Audit code-group frequencies across periods

Source: R/code-audit.R
nis_audit_code_transition.Rd

Counts discharges matching each named code-prefix group by period. A discharge is counted once per group, even when multiple slots match. Prefix matching follows nis_flag_pr() or nis_flag_dx(), according to type. The complete grid of observed periods and code groups is returned, with zero counts where a group has no matches. Counts apply only to the selected code system; zero does not mean the code is absent under another system. Audits across the 2015 ICD transition need separate calls for each system. The change compares with the previous observed period in sorted order.

Usage

nis_audit_code_transition(
  .data,
  codes,
  cohort = NULL,
  by = "YEAR",
  type = c("pr", "dx"),
  system = c("icd10", "icd9"),
  weight_var = "DISCWT",
  output = c("summary", "inventory"),
  sparse_n = 10L
)

Arguments

.data

A data frame or lazy DuckDB query.

codes

A named character vector or named list of character vectors. Each name is a code_group; each value contains prefixes. Names must be non-empty and unique.

cohort

Optional tidy-evaluation logical expression defining the cohort. Rows where it evaluates to NA are excluded.

by

Names of one or more existing columns defining periods, with no duplicates.

type

Whether to match diagnosis ("dx") or procedure ("pr") slots.

system

Code system of the slots: "icd10" (default) or "icd9".

weight_var

Name of the survey weight column, defaulting to "DISCWT". Values in the selected cohort must be finite, non-missing numeric values.

output

"summary" (default) for code-group frequencies or "inventory" for observed code matches by period.

sparse_n

Largest unweighted count flagged "sparse" in the inventory. Defaults to 10, matching nis_suppress(). Used only when output = "inventory".

Value

A collected tibble. For output = "summary", the period columns from by, code_group, n_cohort_unweighted, n_unweighted, n_weighted, pct_within_year, and yoy_pct_change. The change is the relative percent change in pct_within_year versus the previous observed period in sorted order. It is NA for the first period, a period with a missing value, when the previous period's percentage is zero, and in every row when by names more than one column. For output = "inventory", the period columns, code_group, code, n_cohort_unweighted, n_unweighted, n_weighted, and status.

Details

by may name several columns, such as c("YEAR", "DQTR"). A period is then one observed combination of their values, sorted by the columns in the order given. A period with a missing value in any component is kept as its own row, sorted after every complete period. Combinations that do not occur in the data are not added. With several columns, no unambiguous year comparison can be inferred, because adjacent combinations may be quarters of one year or the boundary between two other components. yoy_pct_change is therefore NA in every row; compare pct_within_year across the periods you care about instead.

With output = "inventory", the function instead lists the full codes observed in the selected slots that start with each group's prefixes, with unweighted and weighted discharge counts for every period. A discharge is counted once per code, even when the code occupies several slots. Each observed code is listed for every period, so a code that is rare in some periods or missing from them is visible. status is "absent" when the code has no matches in the period, "sparse" when its unweighted count is at least one and at most sparse_n, and "observed" otherwise. A group that matches no observed code is returned with code missing and status "absent" in every period. Counts are aggregated in the database for lazy inputs, so only period-by-code counts are collected, however many codes a prefix matches. The counts are exact, so apply your disclosure rules (see nis_suppress()) before sharing them.

See also

Code transitions and sensitivity.

Other cohort-definition: nis_attrition(), nis_ccsr_codes(), nis_dx_sensitivity(), nis_flag_dx(), nis_flag_dx_position(), nis_flag_pr(), nis_flag_pr_timing(), nis_prday_completeness()

Examples

toy_data <- dplyr::tibble(
  YEAR = c(2018L, 2018L, 2019L, 2019L, 2020L, 2020L),
  I10_PR1 = c("02UG0JZ", "02UG0JZ", "02UG0JZ", "02803ZZ", "02803ZZ", "02803ZZ"),
  DISCWT = rep(5, 6)
)
nis_audit_code_transition(toy_data,
  codes = c(myectomy = "02UG0JZ", ablation = "02803ZZ"))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>    YEAR code_group n_cohort_unweighted n_unweighted n_weighted pct_within_year
#>   <int> <chr>                    <int>        <int>      <dbl>           <dbl>
#> 1  2018 myectomy                     2            2         10             100
#> 2  2019 myectomy                     2            1          5              50
#> 3  2020 myectomy                     2            0          0               0
#> 4  2018 ablation                     2            0          0               0
#> 5  2019 ablation                     2            1          5              50
#> 6  2020 ablation                     2            2         10             100
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: yoy_pct_change <dbl>

# Observed full codes by period, with absent and sparse periods flagged
nis_audit_code_transition(toy_data,
  codes = c(myectomy = "02UG", ablation = "0280"), output = "inventory")
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>    YEAR code_group code    n_cohort_unweighted n_unweighted n_weighted status
#>   <int> <chr>      <chr>                 <int>        <int>      <dbl> <chr> 
#> 1  2018 myectomy   02UG0JZ                   2            2         10 sparse
#> 2  2019 myectomy   02UG0JZ                   2            1          5 sparse
#> 3  2020 myectomy   02UG0JZ                   2            0          0 absent
#> 4  2018 ablation   02803ZZ                   2            0          0 absent
#> 5  2019 ablation   02803ZZ                   2            1          5 sparse
#> 6  2020 ablation   02803ZZ                   2            2         10 sparse

# Periods defined by several columns
toy_data$DQTR <- c(1L, 2L, 1L, 2L, 1L, 2L)
nis_audit_code_transition(toy_data, c(myectomy = "02UG0JZ"),
  by = c("YEAR", "DQTR"))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 8
#>    YEAR  DQTR code_group n_cohort_unweighted n_unweighted n_weighted
#>   <int> <int> <chr>                    <int>        <int>      <dbl>
#> 1  2018     1 myectomy                     1            1          5
#> 2  2018     2 myectomy                     1            1          5
#> 3  2019     1 myectomy                     1            1          5
#> 4  2019     2 myectomy                     1            0          0
#> 5  2020     1 myectomy                     1            0          0
#> 6  2020     2 myectomy                     1            0          0
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: pct_within_year <dbl>, yoy_pct_change <dbl>
